mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises real discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in real GDP growth below 1% for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth < 1% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in these episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index of more than 0.5% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility for cyclicals and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and CPI above their prior 12-month averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock that increases real interest rates and erodes real equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above 0.4% coincident with a decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) below -0.3% signals a shift from durable goods to services spending, which historically precedes a mild equity pullback over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 0.4% AND HOUST monthly change < -0.3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment growth above 1% combined with an unemployment rate below 3.5% signals an overheating labor market that increases the probability of aggressive Fed tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in these episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent quarterly real GDP growth above 4% for three consecutive quarters signals a late-cycle expansion, which historically precedes mean reversion and negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > 4% for 3 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such late-cycle episodes.
